items.desc: These collapsed sheets of metal from the DM-300 have formed together into a rigid cape. It seems to store a deep energy, perhaps it has some of the DM-300's power?

items.name: chalice of blood
items.desc: This shining silver chalice is oddly adorned with sharp gems at the rim.

items.name: cloak of shadows
items.desc:
A priceless magical cloak, stolen from the royal armory many years ago by the Rogue. When worn, it can be used to turn completely invisible for a short time.

The more the cloak is used, the stronger it will become, allowing the Rogue to become invisible more frequently and for longer durations.

items.name: dried rose
items.desc: Is this the rose that the ghost mentioned before disappearing? It seems to hold some spiritual power, perhaps it can be used to channel the energy of that lost warrior.

items.name: ethereal chains
items.desc: These large yet lightweight chains glow with spiritual energy. They can be used to pull you towards terrain, or pull enemies toward you. The ethereal nature of the chains even allows them to extend through walls!

items.name: holy tome
items.desc:
A holy tome that acts as a focus for the Cleric's divine magic. Using the tome lets the Cleric cast a variety of magical spells.

The tome will steadily get more powerful as the Cleric uses it, giving the Cleric more maximum charges and slightly increasing the recharging speed.

items.name: horn of plenty
items.desc: This horn can't be blown into, but instead seems to fill up with food as you adventure and gain experience. You can consume each charge individually as a snack, or eat until you're full.

items.name: lloyd's beacon
items.desc: Lloyd's beacon is an intricate magical device which grants the user control of teleportation magics. The beacon can be used to return to a set location, but can also expel bursts of random teleportation magic once it has charged from being equipped. This magic can be directed at a target or at the user themselves.

items.name: master thieves' armband
items.desc: This purple velvet armband bears the mark of a master thief. This doesn't belong to you, but it probably didn't belong to its last user either.

items.name: scrying orb
items.desc:
A flawless sphere of violet crystal on a bronze stand, its depths swirling with captured starlight. Held in the Mage's off hand it focuses every working of magic he makes.

While it is in the Mage's _off-hand slot_, all of his magical damage is increased by _X%%_: tome spells, wands, the disintegration ray and aura, Elemental Blast, magical skills and traits.

Only a Mage can use it.

items.name: skeleton key
items.desc: An important-looking key with a head shaped like a skull. Its teeth seem to be different every time you look at them.

items.name: talisman of foresight
items.desc: A smooth stone with strange engravings on it. You feel like it's watching everything around you, keeping an eye out for anything hidden.

items.name: timekeeper's hourglass
items.desc: This large ornate hourglass looks fairly unassuming, but you feel a great power in its finely carved frame. As you rotate the hourglass and watch the sand pour you can feel its magic tugging at you, surely using this magic would give you some control over time.

items.name: unstable spellbook
items.desc: This Tome is in surprising good condition given its age. It fizzes and crackles as you move the pages, surging with unstable energy. If you read from this book, there's no telling what spell you might cast.

items.name: ingot
items.desc:
A bar of metal, ready for the anvil. Use it to reforge, enhance or repair gear made of metal.

Umbralite is the rarest metal in the dungeon, pulsing with a faint purple light. It can be _melded_ straight into any weapon, armor, wand, ring or other upgradable item, anywhere: each ingot adds a purple _+1 umbralite level_, up to +5. Umbralite levels are a little stronger than normal upgrades, and they carry over when gear is reforged, but melting the item does not give them back.

Gathered in quantity, it can also be forged into weapons and armor of unmatched quality.

items.name: ore
items.desc: A lump of raw metal ore. Smelt it at a furnace to get an ingot.

items.name: cloth
items.desc: A folded length of cloth cloth. Use it at an anvil to reforge, enhance or repair cloth armor.

items.name: leather
items.desc: A cured piece of leather. Use it at an anvil to reforge, enhance or repair leather armor and whips.

mobs.name: acidic scorpio
mobs.desc: These huge arachnid-like demonic creatures avoid close combat, preferring to fire crippling serrated spikes from long distances. This one appears to be dripping with corrosive ooze.

mobs.name: albino rat
mobs.desc: This is a rare breed of marsupial rat, with pure white fur and jagged teeth.

mobs.name: armored brute
mobs.desc: The most senior gnoll brutes often wear powerful armor to show their status. The armor makes these brutes much more resilient to physical damage, and their greater discipline means they can rage for much longer before succumbing to their wounds.

mobs.name: armored statue
mobs.desc:
You would think that it's just another one of this dungeon's inanimate statues, but its red glowing eyes give it away.

It seems to be in great condition because of the armor it's wearing, it might be very hard to kill.

mobs.name: crazy bandit
mobs.desc:
An elite thief, distinguished by their more opulent purple robe. Despite their greater skill, they've become just as mindless as regular thieves.

In addition to stealing from you, crazed bandits will briefly blind, cripple, and poison you! They're much more likely to be carrying extra loot than a regular thief though.

mobs.name: vampire bat
mobs.desc: These brisk and tenacious inhabitants of the caves are much more dangerous than they seem. They replenish their health with each successful attack, which allows them to defeat much larger opponents.

mobs.name: golden bee
mobs.desc: Despite their small size, golden bees tend to protect their home fiercely. This one is very mad, better keep your distance.

mobs.name: gnoll brute
mobs.desc: Brutes are the largest, strongest, and toughest of all gnolls. When mortally wounded, they go berserk, gaining temporary shielding and a large boost to damage.

mobs.name: caustic slime
mobs.desc: This slime seems to have been tainted by the dark magic emanating from below. It has lost its usual green color, and drips with caustic ooze.

mobs.name: sewer crab
mobs.desc: These huge crabs are at the top of the food chain in the sewers. They are extremely fast and their thick carapace can withstand heavy blows.

mobs.name: crystal mimic
mobs.desc:
Mimics are magical creatures which can take any shape they wish. In dungeons they almost always choose a shape of a treasure chest, in order to lure in unsuspecting adventurers.

Crystal mimics are trickier than their regular cousins, and prefer to avoid conflict while stealing loot. They will attempt to sprint away once discovered, and have the ability to reposition enemies when they attack.
mobs.where: Hides as a chest in any region

mobs.name: DM-100
mobs.desc: The DM-100 is an early model of dwarven 'defense machine' which was designed to protect dwarven miners in the caves below this prison. Their electrical shocks proved too weak however, and so they were gifted to the human city above. They went unused for years and eventually found their way to the prison, where the warden initially deemed them too cruel to use. However, as the prisoners became more unruly they became a necessity.

mobs.name: DM-200
mobs.desc:
The DM-200 is the second generation of dwarven 'defense machine', which was designed to protect dwarven miners in the caves and city below. They are much larger and bulkier than their predecessors, and attack with devastating hydraulic fists.

Their increased size is also their primary weakness, as they are unable to fit into the narrow tunnels and doorways of the dungeon. The dwarves were able to compensate for the DM-200's lack of mobility by allowing them to vent their toxic exhaust fumes at distant enemies, or enemies they cannot reach.

mobs.name: DM-201
mobs.desc:
The dwarves briefly experimented with more heavily emphasizing the DM-200's lack of mobility and created some DM models that are entirely stationary. The DM-201 is a retrofitted DM-200 which acts as a sentry turret that has no movement ability. In exchange for the lack of mobility, DM-201s have significantly more durability and attacking power.

As DM-201s have no engine to vent exhaust from, the dwarves instead outfitted them with corrosive gas grenades! DM-201s are careful with these grenades however, and will only lob them when attacked from a distance.

mobs.name: DM-300
mobs.desc:
The DM-300 is the largest and most powerful 'defense machine' that the dwarves ever built. Such an awesome machine is difficult to manufacture, so the dwarves only ever made a few to guard the entrances to their underground metropolis.

It is equipped with vents to jet its toxic exhaust fumes and a high power drill that it can use both to attack and disrupt the earth. DM-300 can also connect to an energy grid, further enhancing its power.

mobs.name: demon spawner
mobs.desc:
This twisting amalgam of dwarven flesh is responsible for creating ripper demons from the dwarves that have died in this region. Clearly the demons see no issue with using every resource they can against their enemies.

While visually terrifying, demon spawners have no means of moving or directly defending themselves. Their considerable mass makes them hard to kill quickly however, and they will spawn ripper demons more quickly when they are under threat.

_Demon spawners seem to be connected to some central source of demonic power. Killing them may weaken it._

mobs.name: King of Dwarves
mobs.desc:
Many years ago one of the highest wizards in the dwarven court uncovered secrets which gave him tremendous power over life and death. He soon put this power to use, subjugating and corrupting his peers, his king, and eventually every dwarven citizen. Now he is king, ruler over a legion of undead subjects.

The King of Dwarves is an aggressive foe, who will attempt to surround and overwhelm his enemies with his horde of undead minions.

mobs.name: ebony mimic
mobs.desc:
Mimics are magical creatures which can take any shape they wish. In dungeons they almost always choose a shape of a treasure chest, in order to lure in unsuspecting adventurers.

Ebony mimics are stealthy mimics with the ability to make themselves almost invisible. They lurk on things that adventurers are likely to interact with, but do contain loot of their own as well. They aren't any tougher than a regular mimic once discovered, but their surprise bite is devastating.
mobs.where: Hides as a chest in any region

mobs.name: evil eye
mobs.desc:
Evil Eyes are floating balls of pent up demonic energy. While they are capable of melee combat, their true strength comes from their magic.

After building energy for a short time an Evil Eye will unleash a devastating beam of energy called the _deathgaze._ Anything within the Evil Eye's sights will take tremendous damage, wise adventurers will run for cover.

mobs.name: fetid rat
mobs.desc:
Something is clearly wrong with this rat. Its greasy black fur and rotting skin are very different from the healthy rats you've seen previously. Its pale green eyes make it seem especially menacing.

The rat carries a cloud of horrible stench with it, it's overpoweringly strong up close.

Dark ooze dribbles from the rat's mouth, it eats through the floor but seems to dissolve in water.

mobs.name: dwarven ghoul
mobs.desc:
As dwarven society slowly began to collapse, and the current king of the dwarves seized absolute power, those who were weak or who resisted him were not treated well. As the king grew more adept at wielding dark magic, he bent these dwarves to his will, and now they make up the footsoldiers of his army.

Ghouls are not especially strong on their own, but always travel in groups and are much harder to kill in large numbers. _When a ghoul is defeated, it will rise again after a few turns as long as another ghoul is nearby._

mobs.name: gnoll scout
mobs.desc: Gnolls are hyena-like humanoids. They dwell in sewers and dungeons, venturing up to raid the surface from time to time. Gnoll scouts are regular members of their pack, they are not as strong as brutes and not as intelligent as shamans.

mobs.name: gnoll exile
mobs.desc: This grey-furred gnoll has a large mark on its shoulder, denoting it as an exile. Gnolls are usually exiled from their society for ignoring orders or breaking laws. Exiles have to be strong and shrewd to survive, this one looks like it knows how to use the spear it's holding.

mobs.name: gnoll trickster
mobs.desc:
A strange looking creature, even by gnoll standards. It hunches forward with a wicked grin, almost cradling the satchel hanging over its shoulder. Its eyes are wide with a strange mix of fear and excitement.

There is a large collection of poorly made darts in its satchel, they all seem to be tipped with various harmful substances.

mobs.name: golden mimic
mobs.desc:
Mimics are magical creatures which can take any shape they wish. In dungeons they almost always choose a shape of a treasure chest, in order to lure in unsuspecting adventurers.

Golden mimics are tougher mimics which try to attract the strongest adventurers. They have better loot, but are also much stronger than regular mimics.
mobs.where: Hides as a chest in any region

mobs.name: golem
mobs.desc:
Golems are an attempt to correct the previous flaws in dwarven machinery via the dwarves newfound use of magic. They are much more compact and efficient compared to the DM-300 while still being very deadly.

While golems are still too large to fit into passageways, the dwarves have given them new magical abilities to compensate. Golems can teleport themselves between rooms, and teleport enemies to them when they are out of reach.

mobs.name: Goo
mobs.desc:
Little is known about The Goo. It's quite possible that it is not even a creature, but rather a conglomerate of vile substances from the sewers that somehow gained basic intelligence. Regardless, dark magic is certainly what has allowed Goo to exist.

Its gelatinous nature has let it absorb lots of dark energy, you feel a chill just from being near. If Goo is able to attack with this energy you won't live for long.

mobs.name: great crab
mobs.desc:
This crab is gigantic, even compared to other sewer crabs. Its blue shell is covered in cracks and barnacles, showing great age. It lumbers around slowly, barely keeping balance with its massive claw.

While the crab only has one claw, its size easily compensates. The crab holds the claw in front of any threat, shielding itself behind an impenetrable wall of carapace. However, the crab cannot block attacks it doesn't see coming, or attacks from multiple enemies at once.

mobs.name: prison guard
mobs.desc:
Once keepers of the prison, these guards have long since become no different than the inmates. They shamble like zombies, brainlessly roaming through the halls in search of anything out of place, like you!

They carry chains around their hip, possibly used to pull in enemies to close range.

mobs.name: hermit crab
mobs.desc: For one reason or another, this sewer crab has decided to wear the broken upper part of a barrel on its head! The extra weight has slown it down to regular speed, but has also granted it considerably more defence. You think you can hear something bouncing around inside the barrel though...

mobs.name: mimic
mobs.desc:
Mimics are magical creatures which can take any shape they wish. In dungeons they almost always choose a shape of a treasure chest, in order to lure in unsuspecting adventurers.

Mimics have a nasty bite, but often hold more treasure than a regular chest.
mobs.where: Hides as a chest in any region

mobs.name: dwarf monk
mobs.desc:
These monks are fanatics, who have devoted themselves to protecting their king through physical might. So great is their devotion that they have totally surrendered their minds to their king, and now roam the dwarven city like mindless zombies.

Monks rely solely on the art of hand-to-hand combat, and are able to use their unarmed fists both for offense and defense. When they become focused, monks will parry the next physical attack used against them, even if it was otherwise guaranteed to hit. Monks build focus more quickly while on the move, and more slowly when in direct combat.

mobs.name: necromancer
mobs.desc:
These apprentice dark mages have flocked to the prison, as it is the perfect place to practise their evil craft.

Necromancers will summon and empower skeletons to fight for them. Killing the necromancer will also kill the skeleton it summons.

mobs.name: phantom piranha
mobs.desc:
Phantom piranhas are a rare breed of piranha with magical abilities and eerie translucent bodies. They are capable of teleporting as they are being attacked, either to escape or to quickly get close to their enemy!

While they are annoying to fight, their meat is prized for its magical properties.

mobs.name: giant piranha
mobs.desc: These carnivorous fish are bred specifically to protect flooded areas. Their bite is deadly, so it's best to avoid confronting them directly.

mobs.name: marsupial rat
mobs.desc: Marsupial rats are aggressive but rather weak denizens of the sewers. They have a nasty bite, but are only life threatening in large numbers.

mobs.name: ripper demon
mobs.desc:
These horrific creatures are the result of the many dwarven corpses in this region being put to use by demonic forces. Rippers are emaciated ghoulish creatures that resemble dwarves, but with broken bodies and long sharp claws made of bone.

Ripper demons are not particularly durable, but they are agile and dangerous. They are capable of leaping great distances to quickly reach targets before goring them with their claws.

mobs.name: rot heart
mobs.desc: A Rotberry's fruit is very unique. Instead of rotting away and providing nutrients, the fruit grows, hardens, and encompasses the seed. It provides protection for the internal organs which grow inside the fruit. This giant orb is referred to as the heart of an adult rotberry plant.

mobs.name: rot lasher
mobs.desc: The rot lasher is a part of a mature rotberry plant's root structure, and also their primary means of defense. Lashers are blind and stuck into the ground, but will violently assault any nearby threat after taking a moment to detect them. When there is no nearby enemies, they stand motionless, attempting to blend in with surrounding vegetation.

mobs.name: scorpio
mobs.desc: These huge arachnid-like demonic creatures avoid close combat, preferring to fire crippling serrated spikes from long distances.

mobs.name: senior monk
mobs.desc:
These monks are fanatics, who have devoted themselves to protecting their king through physical might. So great is their devotion that they have totally surrendered their minds to their king, and now roam the dwarven city like mindless zombies.

This monk has mastered the art of hand-to-hand combat, and is able to gain focus while moving much more quickly than regular monks. When they become focused, monks will parry the next physical attack used against them, even if it was otherwise guaranteed to hit. Monks build focus more quickly while on the move, and more slowly when in direct combat.

mobs.name: skeleton
mobs.desc: Skeletons are composed of the bones of unlucky adventurers and inhabitants of the prison, animated by emanations of evil magic from the depths below. After they have been damaged enough, skeletons will disintegrate in an explosion of bones. The shrapnel from this explosion is harmful to anything nearby, but armor is very effective at mitigating it.

mobs.name: slime
mobs.desc:
Slimes are strange, slightly magical creatures with a rubbery outer body and a liquid core. The city sewers provide them with an ample supply of water and nutrients.

Because of their elastic outer membrane, it is difficult to deal more than _6 damage_ to slimes from any one attack.

mobs.name: sewer snake
mobs.desc:
These oversized serpents are capable of quickly slithering around blows, making them quite hard to hit. Magical attacks or surprise attacks are capable of catching them off-guard however.

You can perform a surprise attack by attacking while out of the snake's vision. One way is to let a snake chase you through a doorway and then _strike just after it moves into the door._

mobs.name: spectral necromancer
mobs.desc:
While Skeletons are a necromancer’s bread and butter, some prefer to look into other less corporeal minions. Spectral necromancers have chosen wraiths as their minion of choice!

Individual wraiths aren't as strong as skeletons, but these necromancers aren't afraid to summon a bunch of them!

mobs.name: cave spinner
mobs.desc: These greenish furry cave spiders try to avoid direct combat. Instead they prefer to wait in the distance while their victim struggles in their excreted cobweb, slowly dying from their venomous bite. They are capable of shooting their webs great distances, and will try to block whatever path their prey is taking.

mobs.name: animated statue
mobs.desc: You would think that it's just another one of this dungeon's inanimate statues, but its red glowing eyes give it away.

mobs.name: succubus
mobs.desc:
Succubi are shapeshifting demons that manipulate the minds of their prey. This one has taken the form of a pale gothic humanoid, perhaps to attract dwarven warlocks?

Succubi may temporarily charm their enemy when they attack, making their enemy unable to directly attack them. When succubi attack a charmed enemy, they will steal some of their life essence.

mobs.name: swarm of flies
mobs.desc: The deadly swarm of flies buzzes angrily. Every non-magical attack will split it into two smaller but equally dangerous swarms.

mobs.name: Tengu
mobs.desc:
A famous and enigmatic assassin, named for the mask grafted to his face.

Tengu is held down with large clasps on his wrists and knees, though he seems to have gotten rid of his chains long ago.

He will try to use traps, deceptive magic, and precise attacks to eliminate the only thing stopping his escape: you.

mobs.name: crazy thief
mobs.desc:
Though these inmates roam free of their cells, this place is still their prison. Over time, this place has taken their minds as well as their freedom. Long ago, these crazy thieves and bandits have forgotten who they are and why they steal.

These enemies are more likely to steal and run than they are to fight. Make sure to keep them in sight, or you might never see your stolen item again.

mobs.name: tormented spirit
mobs.desc:
Tormented spirits are otherwise good-natured spirits that have been afflicted by a curse. So long as they are cursed they will attack just like a wraith, and are more powerful as well!

It may be possible to cleanse the curse by using the right item while next to the spirit. If the curse is lifted the spirit will surely be grateful...

mobs.name: dwarf warlock
mobs.desc:
As the dwarves' interests shifted from engineering to arcane arts, warlocks came to power in the city. They started with elemental magic, but soon switched to demonology and necromancy. The strongest of these warlocks seized the throne of the dwarven city, and his cohorts were allowed to continue practising their dark magic, so long as they surrendered their free will to him.

These warlocks possess powerful disruptive magic, and are able to temporarily hinder the upgrade magic applied to your equipment. The more upgraded an item is, the more strongly it will be affected.

mobs.name: wraith
mobs.desc: A wraith is a vengeful spirit of a sinner, whose grave or tomb was disturbed. Being an ethereal entity, it is very hard to hit with a regular weapon.

mobs.name: Yog-Dzewa
mobs.desc:
Yog-Dzewa is an Old God; a great monstrosity which reaches into mortal worlds and devours them to fuel its endless growth. The dwarves must have attracted the attention of this cosmic horror while toying with dark magics, and have been trying to keep it contained ever since.

Yog-Dzewa originates from a dimension of raw magical chaos, and cannot bring its true form into this world. Instead it has created avatars and summoned demonic minions to do its bidding here.

This giant eye is the focal point of Yog-Dzewa's power in this world. While the eye itself is immobile, it is capable of shooting powerful beams of demonic magic and summoning a variety of minions to aid it.

mobs.name: modified DM-100
mobs.desc:
These DM-100s look almost identical to ones you'd find in the prison, but with a bright teal glow coming from their eye. Probably they have been retrofitted to use some more modern dwarven power source.

They act just like regular DM-100s. Their ability to arc lightning at a distance is still present despite the power source change, and their cleaner condition makes them a bit more durable.

mobs.name: modified DM-200
mobs.desc:
These DM-200s look just like their counterparts from the caves, but with glowing teal eyes. They have probably been retrofitted with a more modern dwarven power source.

Just like in their caves counterparts, these DM-200s are too large to fit into enclosed spaces, and are still capable of spewing gas.

mobs.name: dwarven skeleton
mobs.desc:
These would look like normal skeletons from the prison if it weren't for their stunning amount of facial hair. It seems like some dwarves weren't above necromancy even before their new King took over.

They act just like regular skeletons, including exploding into bone shards on death. Paradoxically, their beards seem to offer them a little more protection too.

mobs.name: anvil
mobs.desc: A heavy iron anvil. With the right materials you can reforge, enhance and repair your gear here.

mobs.name: troll blacksmith
mobs.desc: This troll blacksmith looks like all trolls look: he is tall and lean, and his skin resembles stone in both color and texture. The troll blacksmith is tinkering with disproportionally small tools.

mobs.name: furnace
mobs.desc: A squat stone furnace burning hot enough to melt metal. It can melt down unwanted weapons and armor into raw materials, and smelt ore into ingots.

mobs.name: sad ghost
mobs.desc: The ghost is barely visible. It looks like a shapeless spot of faint light with a sorrowful face.

mobs.name: ambitious imp
mobs.desc:
This little red person look like an Imp. Imps are lesser demons, notable for their intelligence and not their strength.

You've only heard about demons in ancient folk tales though, which usually describe them as travelers from another world. You've never seen any evidence demons actually exist, but this Imp is clearly real and seems very happy to see you.

mobs.name: ambitious imp
mobs.desc: The imp has set up a little shop on the border of the inner halls. It's nice to see a friendly face, but his prices certainly don't seem friendly.

mobs.name: mirror image
mobs.desc:
This illusion bears a close resemblance to you, even seeming to wield your current weapon and armor.

Mirror images will seek and attack enemies using their mimicked weapon, which behaves the same as yours, but deals less damage. They start out nearly invisible, but must take on a form that's more easily seen in order to attack.

While their offensive power can be potent, mirror images have no durability, and will fade the moment they take damage.

mobs.name: prismatic image
mobs.desc:
This shimmering illusion bears a close resemblance to you, even seeming to wield your current weapon and armor.

Prismatic images will attempt to seek and draw focus from enemies, using their enhanced defense and health to protect you. While they do not have the same offensive power as mirror images, they have enhanced durability, including receiving benefits from your armor.

When reduced to 0 hp, prismatic images will fade over several turns, and can still be healed during this time. When no enemies are present, prismatic images will fade and rejoin their master.

mobs.name: rat king
mobs.desc: This rat is a little bigger than a regular marsupial rat. It's wearing a tiny crown on its head.

mobs.name: sheep
mobs.desc: This is a magic sheep. What's so magical about it? You can't kill it. It will stand there until it magically fades away, all the while chewing cud with a blank stare.

mobs.name: shopkeeper
mobs.desc: This stout guy looks more appropriate for a trade district in some large city than for a dungeon. His prices explain why he prefers to do business here.

mobs.name: old wandmaker
mobs.desc: This old yet hale gentleman wears a slightly confused expression. He is protected by a magic shield.

skills.name: Cleave
skills.desc: Hit every adjacent enemy for 80 / 100 / 120% damage.

skills.name: Riposte Stance
skills.desc: For 2 turns, melee attacks against you are parried and countered for 100 / 125 / 150% damage.

skills.name: Blade Discipline
skills.desc: +5 / 10 / 15% accuracy with swords, and with daggers too.

skills.name: Momentum
skills.desc: Each hit in a row on the same target adds +4 / 6 / 8% damage, up to 5 stacks.

skills.name: Thousand Cuts
skills.desc: Strike one adjacent enemy 6 times in a single turn at 60% damage each. Every hit can trigger enchantments.

skills.name: Backstab
skills.desc: Blink behind an adjacent enemy and strike for 150 / 175 / 200% damage, always as a sneak attack.

skills.name: Fan of Knives
skills.desc: Throw 3 / 4 / 5 phantom blades at nearby enemies, each for 50% damage.

skills.name: Lacerate
skills.desc: Hits have 15 / 25 / 35% chance to cause bleeding. Backstab always does.

skills.name: Shadow Step
skills.desc: After a kill, you are invisible for 1 / 2 / 3 turns.

skills.name: Death Mark
skills.desc: Mark a target for 10 turns: it takes +50% damage from you, and killing it resets Backstab.

skills.name: Sunder
skills.desc: A heavy chop for 130 / 150 / 170% damage that strips 30 / 45 / 60% of the target's armor for 10 turns.

skills.name: Whirlwind
skills.desc: Spin and hit every enemy around you for 90 / 110 / 130% damage, knocking them back.

skills.name: Bloodlust
skills.desc: +1% damage for every 3 / 2.5 / 2% of HP you are missing, up to +30%.

skills.name: Executioner
skills.desc: +25 / 40 / 55% damage against enemies below 30% HP. Kills with it lower Sunder's cooldown by 3 turns.

skills.name: Rampage
skills.desc: For 8 turns: +40% damage, hits heal you for 10% of damage dealt, and kills extend Rampage by 2 turns.

skills.name: Skull Crack
skills.desc: A blow for 120 / 135 / 150% damage that stuns for 2 / 3 / 3 turns (bosses: 1).

skills.name: Ground Slam
skills.desc: Enemies within 2 tiles take 70 / 90 / 110% damage and are crippled for 3 turns.

skills.name: Crushing Weight
skills.desc: Your hits ignore 15 / 30 / 45% of enemy armor.

skills.name: Concussive
skills.desc: Hits have 8 / 12 / 16% chance to daze. Dazed or stunned enemies take +20% damage from your blunt skills.

skills.name: Earthshaker
skills.desc: Every enemy in view takes 150% damage and is stunned for 2 turns. The quake reveals hidden doors and traps nearby and caves in the ordinary walls right next to you (never on boss floors or into special rooms).

skills.name: Impale
skills.desc: Thrust through a line of up to 2 / 3 / 3 enemies for 110 / 125 / 140% damage each.

skills.name: Sweep
skills.desc: A wide arc hitting 3 tiles in front of you for 80 / 95 / 110% damage, pushing enemies back.

skills.name: Hold the Line
skills.desc: Enemies that step next to you take a free hit for 40 / 60 / 80% damage.

skills.name: Long Reach
skills.desc: +10 / 20 / 30% damage against enemies 2 tiles away.

skills.name: Reaping Storm
skills.desc: For 5 turns, every enemy that comes within your reach is hit automatically for 100% damage.

skills.name: Arcane Strike
skills.desc: A hit for 100 / 120 / 140% damage that also releases a burst of arcane force into the target.

skills.name: Ward
skills.desc: Gain shielding equal to 15 / 20 / 25% of your max HP for 10 turns.

skills.name: Channeling
skills.desc: Wands recharge 10 / 20 / 30% faster while you wield a staff weapon.

skills.name: Deflection
skills.desc: Staff block +1 / 2 / 3, and 10 / 15 / 20% less magic damage while Ward is up.

skills.name: Arcane Overload
skills.desc: For 6 turns, every melee hit also fires your wand's effect, and zaps cost no charge.

skills.name: Flurry
skills.desc: Three quick strikes at 60 / 70 / 80% damage each, in the time of one attack.

skills.name: Uppercut
skills.desc: A rising blow for 130 / 150 / 170% damage that knocks the target back and dazes it.

skills.name: Combo Counter
skills.desc: Each hit adds a combo point (max 10), each worth +2 / 3 / 4% damage. They fade after 3 turns without hitting.

skills.name: Footwork
skills.desc: +5 / 10 / 15% evasion. After dodging, your next hit deals +30% damage.

skills.name: Hundred Fists
skills.desc: Spend all combo points: one strike per point at 70% damage, all in one turn.

skills.name: Shield Bash
skills.desc: A bash for 90 / 110 / 130% damage plus your shield's block, stunning for 1 / 2 / 2 turns.

skills.name: Bulwark
skills.desc: For 3 / 4 / 5 turns, block twice your shield's block value and ignore knockback.

skills.name: Thorns
skills.desc: Reflect 10 / 20 / 30% of the damage your shield blocks back at the attacker.

skills.name: Steadfast
skills.desc: +1 / 2 / 3 armor. While Bulwark is up, Thorns reflects double.

skills.name: Aegis
skills.desc: For 5 turns you are immune to physical damage, and every block charges a burst that hits all adjacent enemies when Aegis ends.

skills.name: Lash Pull
skills.desc: Yank an enemy up to 3 / 4 / 5 tiles toward you for 80% damage, crippling it.

skills.name: Chain Spin
skills.desc: Hit all enemies within 2 tiles for 70 / 85 / 100% damage.

skills.name: Entangle
skills.desc: Hits have 10 / 15 / 20% chance to root the target for 2 turns. Lash Pull always roots.

skills.name: Wild Swing
skills.desc: Your attacks ignore 10 / 20 / 30% of enemy evasion.

skills.name: Grand Lasso
skills.desc: Pull every enemy in view next to you, root them for 3 turns, then hit them all.

skills.name: Piercing Shot
skills.desc: A shot that passes through every enemy in a line for 100 / 120 / 140% damage.

skills.name: Volley
skills.desc: Fire 3 / 4 / 5 projectiles at random enemies in view, each for 60% damage.

skills.name: Steady Aim
skills.desc: +5 / 10 / 15% accuracy and +10 / 20 / 30% damage against enemies 4 or more tiles away.

skills.name: Recovery
skills.desc: Thrown weapons wear 20 / 35 / 50% slower, and have a 10 / 20 / 30% chance to land back at your feet after a throw.

skills.name: Rain of Arrows
skills.desc: Mark a 5x5 area: for 4 turns, every enemy inside takes 80% damage each turn.

skills.name: Overcharge
skills.desc: Your next zap costs no charge and deals 150 / 175 / 200% damage.

skills.name: Elemental Infusion
skills.desc: For 8 turns, weapon hits deal 20 / 30 / 40% bonus damage and carry your last wand's element: fire can ignite, frost chills, lightning arcs to a nearby enemy, corrosion eats armor, blast wave knocks back, corruption weakens, prismatic light blinds, regrowth roots, transfusion heals you, living earth hardens your skin and disintegration hits harder.

skills.name: Attunement
skills.desc: +1 / 2 / 3 max charges on all wands (up to 10).

skills.name: Resonance
skills.desc: Zapping a target hit by a different wand in the last 3 turns deals +15 / 25 / 35% damage.

skills.name: Spell Fusion
skills.desc: Mage only. Your next zap fires two wands at once, fusing their effects.

skills.name: Spell Weaving
skills.desc: Tome passive. Casting a tome spell brings your other spells _1 / 2 / 3 turns_ closer to ready.

skills.name: Quickened Cast
skills.desc: Tome active. Your next tome spell doesn't go on cooldown at all.

skills.name: Arcane Mastery
skills.desc: Tome passive. Your tome spells deal _5% / 10% / 15%_ more damage.

skills.name: Searing Script
skills.desc: Tome passive. Your tome spells have a _10% / 20% / 30%_ chance to set their target on fire.

skills.name: Rimed Script
skills.desc: Tome passive. Your tome spells have a _10% / 20% / 30%_ chance to chill their target for 4 turns.

heroes.name: warrior
heroes.desc:
The Warrior starts with a _unique broken seal_ that grants him a burst of shielding when he is below half health. The seal can be moved between armors, and can _transfer a single upgrade_ with it.

The Warrior also starts with a _worn shortsword_, _three throwing stones_, cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Warrior endures extra damage with shielding granted by his _broken seal._ The seal can be moved between armors and _transfers a single upgrade._

subclasses.name: juggernaut
subclasses.desc:
The Juggernaut is strong enough to swing _heavy weapons in one hand_: greatswords, greataxes, war hammers, mauls, polearms, staves and chained flails all leave his off hand free for a shield.

The Juggernaut gains rage as he takes physical damage, including damage that gets blocked by his armor! Rage steadily fades away over time, but fades more slowly if he is at low HP.

Rage can cause the Juggernaut to deal up to +50% damage. At max rage he can go berserk, gaining a burst of shielding and keeping his rage as long as he has shielding left. The shielding scales with the level of the juggernaut's armor, and can be massively boosted if he is at low health. The Juggernaut needs time to recover after he goes berserk.

subclasses.name: gladiator
subclasses.desc:
The Gladiator builds one point of combo every time he makes a successful attack with a melee or thrown weapon. If the Gladiator does not make a successful attack within 5 turns (15 turns after a kill), his combo is reset.

As he builds combo the Gladiator can use a variety of abilities that are guaranteed to hit:
2 Combo: knock enemy back, preserves combo
4 Combo: deal damage based on armor
6 Combo: parry, preserves combo
8 Combo: damage target and nearby enemies
10 Combo: attack once for each combo

heroes.name: mage
heroes.desc:
The Mage starts with a _magic tome_ held open in his hand. It casts _magic missiles_, a _fireball_ and a _ray of frost_, each with its own cooldown instead of charges. Spare tomes found in the dungeon can be _deciphered_ to teach him new spells or strengthen known ones. Wands still work alongside the tome.

The Mage also starts with cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Mage is an arcane expert who carries a _magic tome_. He casts spells from it, each with its own cooldown, and can learn new ones.
heroes.unlock: To unlock the Mage _enhance or infuse an item at an anvil._

subclasses.name: battlemage
subclasses.desc:
The Battlemage's power is his own, not his tome's.

_Disintegration Ray:_ an ability he can fire at any time from the action button, with or without a tome. A volatile beam tears through everything in a line; each enemy hit has a _10% chance to be disintegrated outright_ (never bosses). It recharges over 20 turns.

_Disintegration Aura:_ always on. Magic bolts can't hurt him, and every enemy next to him loses a slice of its maximum health each turn.

Both grow stronger as he levels up.

subclasses.name: warlock
subclasses.desc:
The Warlock has a chance to inflict a soul mark on characters when he uses wands on them. The chance to apply a soul mark and its duration increase with wand level.

When an enemy is soul marked, the Warlock will heal 2 hp for every 5 damage he deals to them, but only with attacks from melee or thrown weapons, not from wands!

heroes.name: rogue
heroes.desc:
The Rogue starts with a _unique Cloak of Shadows_, which he can use to become invisible at will.

The Rogue can _detect secrets and traps_ from a greater distance.

The Rogue also starts with _a dagger_, _three throwing knives_, cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Rogue can evade enemies and strike from invisibility using his _cloak of shadows._ He also _detects secrets and traps_ from a greater distance.
heroes.unlock: To unlock the Rogue _perform 10 surprise attacks in one game._

subclasses.name: assassin
subclasses.desc:
The Assassin prepares his next strike when he becomes invisible. The longer he prepares for, the more powerful his next attack will be. Preparation builds for up to 9 turns.

After preparing, the Assassin deals bonus damage on his next attack, can blink to his target, and can even instantly kill enemies who are weak enough.

subclasses.name: freerunner
subclasses.desc:
As the Freerunner moves he builds stacks of momentum. He can gain up to 10 momentum after running for 10 turns, but rapidly loses it if he stops moving. The freerunner can use up his momentum to start freerunning, for 2 turns per point of momentum.

When freerunning the Freerunner moves at 2x speed, and gains bonus evasion in proportion to his level. Once freerunning ends there is a cooldown before momentum can be built again.

heroes.name: huntress
heroes.desc:
The Huntress starts with a _unique spirit bow_, which can fire an infinite number of conjured arrows.

The Huntress can travel through tall grass _without trampling it_.

The Huntress also starts with _studded gloves_, cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Huntress is a master of thrown weapons and has a _magical bow_ with infinite arrows. She also travels through tall grass _without trampling it._
heroes.unlock: To unlock the Huntress _hit enemies with thrown weapons 10 times in one game._

subclasses.name: sniper
subclasses.desc:
The Sniper is a master of ranged combat, whose ranged attacks pierce enemy armor. When she attacks an enemy with a thrown weapon, she places a sniper's mark on them, which lets her follow up with a special attack from her bow. This special attack varies based on how her bow is augmented.

An unaugmented bow will fire a snapshot which deals reduced damage but fires instantly. A speed bow will fire a volley of three arrows which deal reduced damage, can still activate enchantments, and take 1 turn to fire. A damage bow will fire a sniper shot which is guaranteed to hit, deals bonus damage based on distance, and takes 2 turns to fire.

subclasses.name: warden
subclasses.desc:
The Warden has a strong connection to nature which grants her a variety of bonus effects relating to grass and plants. She is able to see through tall and furrowed grass as if it were empty space.

The Warden causes grass to sprout up around any seed she throws or plants, and gains special effects when trampling plants. These special effects replace the regular plant effects, meaning that no plant is harmful for her to step on.

heroes.name: duelist
heroes.desc:
The Duelist starts with a _unique rapier_ and is a master of every weapon: she trains _proficiency in every weapon family 25% faster_, unlocking weapon skills sooner than anyone else.

The Duelist also starts with _two throwing spikes_, cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Duelist is a weapons master who can use her weapon to trigger a _special weapon ability._ This special ability is _different for every weapon._
heroes.unlock: To unlock the Duelist _equip a medium or heavy weapon._

subclasses.name: champion
subclasses.desc:
The Champion is a master of melee weapons who can equip a secondary weapon in addition to her primary one. Her regular attacks use her primary weapon, but she can swap her primary weapon instantly and use either weapon's ability.

She also gains 2 more max weapon ability charges and +50% weapon ability recharge speed.

subclasses.name: monk
subclasses.desc:
The Monk is a master of physical technique. As she defeats enemies, she gains energy which can be used on a variety of defensive and utility-focused abilities. This energy does not fade over time, but has a cap based on the Monk's level.

1 Energy: quickly strike with fists
2 Energy: focus to dodge next attack
3 Energy: instantly dash nearby
4 Energy: kick an enemy away
5 Energy: meditate to clear statuses and restore wand & artifact charge

heroes.name: cleric
heroes.desc:
The Cleric starts with a _unique holy tome_, which they can use to cast various spells.

The Cleric learns his prayers as he grows in experience: Holy Intuition at level 2, Shield of Light at 3, Recall Inscription at 7, Sunray at 8, Divine Sense at 9, Bless at 10, Cleanse at 13 and Light Reading at 14, each growing stronger a few levels later. His subclass grants its own three prayers. His talents grant other blessings instead.

The Cleric also starts with _a cudgel_, cloth armor, a waterskin, and a velvet pouch.
heroes.short: The Cleric is a divine spellcaster who uses their unique _holy tome_ to channel divine magic. He _learns new prayers and strengthens them as he levels up_, leaving his talents free for other blessings.
heroes.unlock: To unlock the Cleric _fully cleanse the curse on any piece of cursed equipment._

subclasses.name: priest
subclasses.desc:
The Priest gains a variety of new and upgraded spells that emphasize ranged combat and synergy with magical items.

The Priest can cast _Guiding Light_ for free once every 50 turns, illuminates enemies directly targeted by any of their spells, and can consume the illumination debuff with allies, wands, and some artifacts for bonus damage equal to their level + 5.

The Priest also gains the _Radiance_ spell, which dispels darkness and affects all visible enemies, triggering and applying illuminate and briefly stunning them at the cost of 2 charges.

The Priest learns the prayers _Holy Lance, Hallowed Ground and Mnemonic Prayer_ right away; they grow stronger at levels 22 and 25.

subclasses.name: paladin
subclasses.desc:
The Paladin gains a variety of new and upgraded spells that emphasize melee combat and synergy with weapons and armor.

The Paladin's _Holy Weapon_ and _Holy Ward_ spells grant larger bonuses, no longer override existing enchantments and glyphs, and can be extended by casting other spells.

The Paladin also gains the _Smite_ spell, which lets them perform a guaranteed melee hit with bonus damage and enchantment power.

The Paladin learns the prayers _Lay on Hands, Aura of Protection and Wall of Light_ right away; they grow stronger at levels 22 and 25.
